key_concept: $Br_2$ adds anti and alkaline $KMnO_4$ adds syn, so the trans- and cis-but-2-enes give products whose meso or racemic nature can be read from the Newman projection.
steps: Expected products: anti addition of $Br_2$ to trans-but-2-ene gives meso-2,3-dibromobutane. Syn dihydroxylation of cis-but-2-ene by cold alkaline $KMnO_4$ gives meso-butane-2,3-diol.

Test for meso in a Newman projection: in the staggered conformation where like groups are anti, the meso form has $Br/Br$ (or $OH/OH$), $Me/Me$ and $H/H$ each anti. That conformation has a centre of symmetry.

Statement I: Br is at $0^\circ$ (front) and $180^\circ$ (back), so the Br atoms are anti. The front Me is at $120^\circ$ and the back Me at $60^\circ$, which is gauche, not anti. Likewise the H atoms at $240^\circ$ and $300^\circ$ are gauche.
So the Statement I structure has no centre of symmetry. It is one enantiomer of the chiral $(\pm)$ dibromide, which comes from cis-but-2-ene, not the meso product. Statement I is incorrect.

Statement II: the front carbon has OH at $0^\circ$, Me at $120^\circ$ and H at $240^\circ$. Rotate the back carbon by $120^\circ$ so that its OH sits at $180^\circ$. Its Me then sits at $300^\circ$ and its H at $60^\circ$.
Now $OH/OH$, $Me/Me$ ($120^\circ$ vs $300^\circ$) and $H/H$ ($240^\circ$ vs $60^\circ$) are all anti. A centre of symmetry exists, so this is meso-butane-2,3-diol. Statement II is correct.
final_answer: Option (4): Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why_not_others: The figure for Statement I shows anti Br atoms, so it looks like anti addition, but its Me groups are gauche. That makes it the chiral (racemic) dibromide rather than the meso product, so options (1) and (3) fail. Statement II correctly shows the meso diol, so option (2) fails.
common_trap: Students see the two Br atoms anti in the Newman projection and conclude it shows the anti-addition (meso) product, without checking whether Me and H are also anti.
time_saving_tip: Remember 'trans + anti → meso' and 'cis + syn → meso'. Then check only whether the two Me groups are anti when the heteroatoms are anti.
